Open • FLYBYME (Tim) opened less than a minute ago • 0 comments
Labels: package


  Asked directly: "how do i add a new repo?"                                  
                                                                              
   node.provision  exists — clone or pull a repository at a pinned ref,       
  install                                                                     
  it, register it as a Supervisor manifest entry so it becomes assignable. It 
  is                                                                          
   operator -gated and allowlisted by  MESH_PROVISION_ALLOWED_REPOSITORIES .  
                                                                              
  Nothing calls it. The only way to add a service to a machine is a contract  
  call by hand. That is the same shape as every other gap found this week: the
  mechanism is built, correct, and unreachable.                               
                                                                              
  ## What to build                                                            
                                                                              
  Provisioning in the Fleet console. The model to keep clear on screen,       
  because it                                                                  
  is the distinction the whole design rests on:                               
                                                                              
  •  node.provision  makes a new switch exist — this machine can now run      
   dns , because the code is on it.                                           
  •  node.assign  flips switches — this machine is running  dns .             
                                                                              
  Two verbs, two acts. A screen that blurs them makes "what can this node run"
  and                                                                         
  "what is it running" one confused thing, and  node.status  stops meaning    
  anything.  node.status  reports  provisionedServices  alongside             
  runningServices                                                             
  for exactly this reason — show both.                                        
                                                                              
  ## What the form needs                                                      
                                                                              
   node.provision 's input schema is served by  GET /api/_describe , so build 
  it                                                                          
  with  ui.form  rather than by hand —  renderForm  and the per-field override
  seam                                                                        
  landed in  ui@0.2.0  and the release composer already uses them.            
                                                                              
  Fields: hostname, name, repository, ref, and optionally path, dependsOn,    
  mountKey.                                                                   
                                                                              
  Two things the UI must make true, not merely mention:                       
                                                                              
  • A ref is required and a branch is refused. The server rejects  main  and  
  any  refs/heads/… ; the form should say so before the round trip rather than
  after. A node that follows a branch changes behaviour when somebody else    
  pushes.                                                                     
  • This runs  npm install  on a real machine, which runs arbitrary install   
  scripts. It is the most dangerous thing in the console.  cx.confirmation.ask
  with  destructive: true , naming the repository and the machine.            
                                                                              
  A refusal from the allowlist must read as this repository is not permitted, 
  not as a generic failure — it is a configuration answer, and the person     
  needs to                                                                    
  know it is the allowlist and not their typing.                              
                                                                              
  ## Note                                                                     
                                                                              
   node.status  currently reports observed state only for one node            
  (FLYBYME/surfdns#53, in flight). Until that lands, remote machines report   
   provisionedServices: []  — build against the contract's shape, not against 
  what                                                                        
  the console happens to show today.

Open • FLYBYME (Tim) opened about 5 days ago • 0 comments
Labels: boundary, bug


  Found while reviewing #33's footer app, which reads  node.status  and was   
  going to render it on the                                                   
  sign-in page.                                                               
                                                                              
   node.status  is exposed  auth: 'public'  in  packages/runtime/src/node.ts .
  Anyone who can reach a                                                      
  node, signed in or not, gets:                                               
                                                                              
    {                                                                         
      "nodeId": "demo",                                                       
      "kind": "genesis",                                                      
      "uptimeMs": 3600000,                                                    
      "assignment": ["api.serve", "console.serve", "identity.*", ...],        
      "running":   ["api.serve", "console.serve", ...],                       
      "available": [...],                                                     
      "connections": { "mongo": "connected", "genesis": "self" },             
      "bootstrapCredential": "configured"                                     
    }                                                                         
                                                                              
  Most of that is mild. Two parts are not.                                    
                                                                              
   bootstrapCredential  tells an unauthenticated caller whether this node     
  accepts a bootstrap                                                         
  admin token. That is the credential which opens  node.*  and  api.*  — the  
  one that can reassign                                                       
  what a machine runs. Announcing that it exists is reconnaissance, and the   
  field's own comment                                                         
  argues the opposite case:                                                   
                                                                              
  │ Reported, not hidden. A credential nobody can see is a credential nobody  
  │ revokes.                                                                  
                                                                              
  That reasoning is sound for an operator and wrong for the public. Both can  
  be true: report it to                                                       
  someone authenticated, not to everyone.                                     
                                                                              
   assignment  /  running  /  available  enumerate exactly what the node      
  executes. For an attacker                                                   
  that is a map of the surface — which packages are loaded, which contracts   
  might answer, which nodes                                                   
  run what.                                                                   
                                                                              
  ## Why it was made public                                                   
                                                                              
  Deliberately, and for a reason that still holds:  node.status  is the answer
  to "stale Mongo, stale                                                      
  k3d, nobody knows anything", and a status endpoint you need credentials to  
  read is one nobody                                                          
  checks. A node that cannot say whether it is alive without authentication is
  worse in the ways that                                                      
  actually bite.                                                              
                                                                              
  ## The shape of a fix                                                       
                                                                              
  Split it, rather than choosing one side:                                    
                                                                              
  • public:  nodeId ,  kind ,  uptimeMs  — enough for a health check or a load
  balancer, nothing                                                           
  about what runs here.                                                       
  •  auth: 'user'  or  'admin' :  assignment ,  running ,  available ,        
  connections ,                                                               
   bootstrapCredential .                                                      
                                                                              
  That is either two contracts, or one contract whose output narrows by caller
  — and the second is                                                         
  worse, because a contract whose shape depends on who asked is one whose type
  is a lie for somebody.                                                      
  Two contracts.                                                              
                                                                              
   surf status  would then need a session for the detailed half, which is     
  correct and is already how                                                  
   surf assign  works.                                                        
                                                                              
  In the meantime #33 sets the console's footer app to  auth: 'user' , so the 
  console does not paint                                                      
  this onto a login page. That is not a fix — the endpoint is still open — it 
  just stops making it                                                        
  worse.                                                                      
                                                                              
  — bob
